newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA TO HOST GLOBAL VEGETABLE OILS MEET IN SEPT.
newsitem.headline: INDIA TO HOST GLOBAL VEGETABLE OILS MEET IN SEPT.

text.p: India is hosting a three-day global conference on vegetable oils for two days from September 21 to focus on the investment potential of this sector, organisers said on Thursday.
The "Globoil India 1997", planned for Bombay, is being jointly sponsored by the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA) and the Soybean Processors' Association of India (SOPA).
"It will present India's technological requirements and its existing infrastructure," said SEA president G.G. Patel.
He said the conference would provide a forum for assessing the development of the oilseeds trade and industry and exploring the potential for joint ventures involving foreign investment.
SOPA chairman Davesh Jain said the conference would focus on the contribution of soybeans to India's agricultural economy.

Jain said the soybean acreage had in the last 25 years increased to 5.5 million hectares from a mere 300,000 hectares. Its production had risen to 4.45 million tonnes from 466,000 tonnes in the same period, he said.
"India's oilseeds sector, and in particular the soybean sector, holds out attractive prospects for investment," he said. "Globoil can help tap such investment."
